clauses.normalized_text: QUIC is a multiplexed and secure transport protocol that runs on top of UDP.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC is a multiplexed and secure transport protocol that runs on top of UDP.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC aims to provide a flexible set of features that allow it to be a general-purpose transport for multiple applications.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC aims to provide a flexible set of features that allow it to be a general-purpose transport for multiple applications.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements techniques learned from experience with TCP, SCTP and other transport protocols.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements techniques learned from experience with TCP, SCTP and other transport protocols.

clauses.normalized_text: Using UDP as the substrate, QUIC seeks to be compatible with legacy clients and middleboxes.
clauses.raw_text: Using UDP as the substrate, QUIC seeks to be compatible with legacy clients and middleboxes.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC authenticates all of its headers and encrypts most of the data it exchanges, including its signaling.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC authenticates all of its headers and encrypts most of the data it exchanges, including its signaling.

clauses.normalized_text: This allows the protocol to evolve without incurring a dependency on upgrades to middleboxes.
clauses.raw_text: This allows the protocol to evolve without incurring a dependency on upgrades to middleboxes.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC relies on a combined cryptographic and transport handshake for setting up a secure transport connection.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC relies on a combined cryptographic and transport handshake for setting up a secure transport connection.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC connections are expected to commonly use 0-RTT handshakes, meaning that for most QUIC connections, data can be sent immediately following the client handshake packet, without waiting for a reply from the server.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC connections are expected to commonly use 0-RTT handshakes, meaning that for most QUIC connections, data can be sent immediately following the client handshake packet, without waiting for a reply from the server.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC provides a dedicated stream (Stream ID 1) to be used for performing the cryptographic handshake and QUIC options negotiation.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC provides a dedicated stream (Stream ID 1) to be used for performing the cryptographic handshake and QUIC options negotiation.

clauses.normalized_text: The format of the QUIC options and parameters used during negotiation are described in this document, but the handshake protocol that runs on Stream ID 1 is described in the accompanying cryptographic handshake draft [QUIC-TLS].
clauses.raw_text: The format of the QUIC options and parameters used during negotiation are described in this document, but the handshake protocol that runs on Stream ID 1 is described in the accompanying cryptographic handshake draft [QUIC-TLS].

clauses.normalized_text: When application messages are transported over TCP, independent application messages can suffer from head-of-line blocking.
clauses.raw_text: When application messages are transported over TCP, independent application messages can suffer from head-of-line blocking.

clauses.normalized_text: When an application multiplexes many streams atop TCP's single-bytestream abstraction, a loss of a TCP segment results in blocking of all subsequent segments until a retransmission arrives, irrespective of the application streams that are encapsulated in subsequent segments.
clauses.raw_text: When an application multiplexes many streams atop TCP's single-bytestream abstraction, a loss of a TCP segment results in blocking of all subsequent segments until a retransmission arrives, irrespective of the application streams that are encapsulated in subsequent segments.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC ensures that lost packets carrying data for an individual stream only impact that specific stream.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC ensures that lost packets carrying data for an individual stream only impact that specific stream.

clauses.normalized_text: Data received on other streams can continue to be reassembled and delivered to the application.
clauses.raw_text: Data received on other streams can continue to be reassembled and delivered to the application.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC's packet framing and acknowledgments carry rich information that help both congestion control and loss recovery in fundamental ways.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC's packet framing and acknowledgments carry rich information that help both congestion control and loss recovery in fundamental ways.
clauses.section_heading: Rich Signaling for Congestion Control and Loss Recovery

clauses.normalized_text: Each QUIC packet carries a new packet number, including those carrying retransmitted data.
clauses.raw_text: Each QUIC packet carries a new packet number, including those carrying retransmitted data.
clauses.section_heading: Rich Signaling for Congestion Control and Loss Recovery

clauses.normalized_text: This obviates the need for a separate mechanism to distinguish acknowledgments for retransmissions from those for original transmissions, avoiding TCP's retransmission ambiguity problem.
clauses.raw_text: This obviates the need for a separate mechanism to distinguish acknowledgments for retransmissions from those for original transmissions, avoiding TCP's retransmission ambiguity problem.
clauses.section_heading: Rich Signaling for Congestion Control and Loss Recovery

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC acknowledgments also explicitly encode the delay between the receipt of a packet and its acknowledgment being sent, and together with the monotonically-increasing packet numbers, this allows for precise network roundtrip-time (RTT) calculation.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC acknowledgments also explicitly encode the delay between the receipt of a packet and its acknowledgment being sent, and together with the monotonically-increasing packet numbers, this allows for precise network roundtrip-time (RTT) calculation.
clauses.section_heading: Rich Signaling for Congestion Control and Loss Recovery

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC's ACK frames support up to 256 ACK blocks, so QUIC is more resilient to reordering than TCP with SACK support, as well as able to keep more bytes on the wire when there is reordering or loss.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC's ACK frames support up to 256 ACK blocks, so QUIC is more resilient to reordering than TCP with SACK support, as well as able to keep more bytes on the wire when there is reordering or loss.
clauses.section_heading: Rich Signaling for Congestion Control and Loss Recovery

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC implements stream- and connection-level flow control, closely following HTTP/2's flow control mechanisms.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC implements stream- and connection-level flow control, closely following HTTP/2's flow control mechanisms.

clauses.normalized_text: At a high level, a QUIC receiver advertises the absolute byte offset within each stream up to which the receiver is willing to receive data.
clauses.raw_text: At a high level, a QUIC receiver advertises the absolute byte offset within each stream up to which the receiver is willing to receive data.

clauses.normalized_text: As data is sent,
clauses.raw_text: As data is sent,

clauses.normalized_text: received, and delivered on a particular stream, the receiver sends WINDOW_UPDATE frames that increase the advertised offset limit for that stream, allowing the peer to send more data on that stream.
clauses.raw_text: received, and delivered on a particular stream, the receiver sends WINDOW_UPDATE frames that increase the advertised offset limit for that stream, allowing the peer to send more data on that stream.

clauses.normalized_text: In addition to this stream-level flow control, QUIC implements connection-level flow control to limit the aggregate buffer that a QUIC receiver is willing to allocate to all streams on a connection.
clauses.raw_text: In addition to this stream-level flow control, QUIC implements connection-level flow control to limit the aggregate buffer that a QUIC receiver is willing to allocate to all streams on a connection.

clauses.normalized_text: Connection-level flow control works in the same way as stream-level flow control, but the bytes delivered and highest received offset are all aggregates across all streams.
clauses.raw_text: Connection-level flow control works in the same way as stream-level flow control, but the bytes delivered and highest received offset are all aggregates across all streams.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP headers appear in plaintext on the wire and are not authenticated, causing a plethora of injection and header manipulation issues for TCP, such as receive-window manipulation and sequence-number overwriting.
clauses.raw_text: TCP headers appear in plaintext on the wire and are not authenticated, causing a plethora of injection and header manipulation issues for TCP, such as receive-window manipulation and sequence-number overwriting.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: While some of these are mechanisms used by middleboxes to improve TCP performance, others are active attacks.
clauses.raw_text: While some of these are mechanisms used by middleboxes to improve TCP performance, others are active attacks.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: Even "performance-enhancing" middleboxes that routinely interpose on the transport state machine end up limiting the evolvability of the transport protocol, as has been observed in the design of MPTCP [RFC6824] and in its subsequent deployability issues.
clauses.raw_text: Even "performance-enhancing" middleboxes that routinely interpose on the transport state machine end up limiting the evolvability of the transport protocol, as has been observed in the design of MPTCP [RFC6824] and in its subsequent deployability issues.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: Generally, QUIC packets are always authenticated and the payload is typically fully encrypted.
clauses.raw_text: Generally, QUIC packets are always authenticated and the payload is typically fully encrypted.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: The parts of the packet header which are not encrypted are still authenticated by the receiver, so as to thwart any packet injection or manipulation by third parties.
clauses.raw_text: The parts of the packet header which are not encrypted are still authenticated by the receiver, so as to thwart any packet injection or manipulation by third parties.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: Some early handshake packets, such as the Version Negotiation packet, are not encrypted, but information sent in these unencrypted handshake packets is later verified as part of cryptographic processing.
clauses.raw_text: Some early handshake packets, such as the Version Negotiation packet, are not encrypted, but information sent in these unencrypted handshake packets is later verified as part of cryptographic processing.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: PUBLIC_RESET packets that reset a connection are currently not authenticated.
clauses.raw_text: PUBLIC_RESET packets that reset a connection are currently not authenticated.
clauses.section_heading: Authenticated and Encrypted Header and Payload

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC connections are identified by a 64-bit Connection ID, randomly generated by the client.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC connections are identified by a 64-bit Connection ID, randomly generated by the client.
clauses.section_heading: Connection Migration and Resilience to NAT Rebinding

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC's consistent connection ID allows connections to survive changes to the client's IP and port, such as those caused by NAT rebindings or by the client changing network connectivity to a new address.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC's consistent connection ID allows connections to survive changes to the client's IP and port, such as those caused by NAT rebindings or by the client changing network connectivity to a new address.
clauses.section_heading: Connection Migration and Resilience to NAT Rebinding

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC provides automatic cryptographic verification of a rebound client, since the client continues to use the same session key for encrypting and decrypting packets.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC provides automatic cryptographic verification of a rebound client, since the client continues to use the same session key for encrypting and decrypting packets.
clauses.section_heading: Connection Migration and Resilience to NAT Rebinding

clauses.normalized_text: The consistent connection ID can be used to allow migration of the connection to a new server IP address as well, since the Connection ID remains consistent across changes in the client's and the server's network addresses.
clauses.raw_text: The consistent connection ID can be used to allow migration of the connection to a new server IP address as well, since the Connection ID remains consistent across changes in the client's and the server's network addresses.
clauses.section_heading: Connection Migration and Resilience to NAT Rebinding
